messages:
maria-support: FYI raised from a customer — p99 for galena-1.2 jumped after yesterday's tokenizer push. They're seeing timeouts on long docs (>12k tokens). Ticket attached.

alex-eng: Can you paste a sample request/trace id so we can correlate with logs?

maria-support: route: /v1/generate, model=galena-1.2, tokenizer=bpe-v2-normalize, trace_id=trc_0a1b2c3d. Example call:

```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \
  -d '{"model":"galena-1.2","input":"<~15k tokens>","stream":false}'
```

kai-ml: Quick summary from ML side: galena-1.2 included a tokenizer normalization and new merge table that increases subtoken counts for some unicode-heavy docs. That can inflate sequence length and trigger KV cache churn / evictions.

leo-sre: I pulled infra logs for the trace id — saw repeated KVCache::reset spikes aligned with the p99 window. Snippet:

```
[2026-03-15T14:02:12Z] instance=rdw-galena-pool-7 model=galena-1.2 KVCache::reset reason=token_seq_grew length=18000 prev_alloc=10240
[2026-03-15T14:02:13Z] instance=rdw-galena-pool-7 latency=1823ms p99=1.82s route=/v1/generate
```

maria-support: Customer repro steps they posted:
1) POST long doc (~12-18k token equivalence)
2) do a follow-up /v1/chat/stream within 3-8s
3) observe p99 ~1.5-2s and occasional 504s

alex-eng: I ran a local repro with our bench script, `repro_long.sh --model galena-1.2 --input samples/long_15k.txt --reps 25` and saw p99 ~1.7s. Repro script here:

```bash
python tools/repro.py --model galena-1.2 --prompt samples/long_15k.txt --iterations 25
```

kai-ml: Hypothesis: tokenizer change -> token fragmentation -> effective seq length increases -> KV cache window exceeded more often -> thrashing and more expensive attention kernels. Also possible more cache misses in compilation layer (kernel select) due to unusual seq lengths.

alex-eng: Mitigation options we discussed:
- quick rollback tokenizer to bpe-v1 for galena-1.2 (low-risk)
- increase kv cache size / window on galena pools (memory tradeoff)
- apply routing rule: long inputs -> galena-1.1 (stable) until patch
- throttle or reject extreme long requests at edge (customer impact)

deploy-bot: Canary rollback initiated to bpe-v1 on 10% of galena-1.2 traffic. canary_id=can_47589_a

deploy-bot: Canary metrics after 30m: p99 on canary slice dropped from 1.8s -> 520ms, error rate unchanged.

maria-support: Customer asks ETA for global rollback. They want performance restored ASAP.

leo-sre: Plan: full variant rollback tonight at 02:10 UTC pending approvals. Steps:
- disable bpe-v2 in model-config for galena-1.2
- revert tokenizer table on edge/binaries
- add temporary routing policy: if tokens_est > 10k route -> galena-1.1
- monitor KVCache.reset counts, p95/p99, and oom events

kai-ml: We'll also run tokenizer ablation (strip normalization) on a 5k-doc corpus to confirm root cause before reintroducing. If confirmed, we'll update merge table and release bpe-v2-v1compat.

alex-eng: I collected traces and a minimal repro harness. Saved to /tmp/galena_repro_47589.tgz and uploaded to infra logs bucket (s3://rdw-debug/galena/47589).

maria-support: Passing to accounts team to notify the customer of rollback window and mitigation. Keeping them informed.

leo-sre: Full rollback completed at 02:17 UTC. Post-rollback metrics:
- p95: 220ms -> stable
- p99: 1.82s -> 480ms
- KVCache::reset events dropped to baseline

maria-support: Customer confirmed improved performance on their side. They observed their typical p99 ~450ms. :thumbsup:

kai-ml: Action items:
- run tokenizer ablation + create new merge table (owner: kai-ml)
- add long-input routing policy for model-onboard changes (owner: alex-eng)
- add KVCache alerting for sudden resets (owner: leo-sre)

alex-eng: I'll draft the postmortem and include the repro script, logs, and the canary results. Root cause: tokenizer fragmentation increasing seq lengths -> cache thrash -> p99 regression.

maria-support: Thanks everyone — closing after PM writes up and KAM emails customer. :heart:

leo-sre: Posting final graphs to the incident channel in 10m, closing here once validated.
